account:
It is eight on day 1, and I am at town hall for my morning office appointment. I have read today's schedule: mill grain inspection at ten, lunch at home at noon, council letters at one, tea with the dockside neighbour at three, office at half past four, and home at seven. I returned the appointment book to the appointments chest for the secretary.

The unusual thing I can actually establish is a gap in the town's financial records. The secretary has not located an accounts ledger or commitments register, and all four great hall table chests were empty. Neither the secretary nor the builder knows who previously kept the ledger. The accounts review is meeting minutes, not verified accounts. Yesterday I verified 128 emeralds in the treasury, but outstanding obligations remain unverified. This merits investigation, though it is not evidence of theft or a secret undertaking.

The builder has repeatedly asked for specific repair work, but reports no confirmed defects. He says the baker and innkeeper also reported no defects or repair needs. No town repairs or transport have been authorized. Freight previously offered quotations if quantities and destinations become known. The innkeeper wants visitor and meeting numbers to plan rooms and meals, but named no actual occasion or date. These may simply be ordinary efforts to obtain business and plan provisions; I have no evidence linking them to anything concealed.

The secretary is helping with the records search and schedule. I supplied one emerald for stationery and just saw the secretary file a written book, whose contents I have not yet read. The neighbour reported nothing unusual yesterday. I still feel I may be missing something, but no witnessed event yet establishes a hidden plan or its purpose. My best course is to review the filed findings, keep my appointments, and ask residents about their actual activities without treating speculation as fact.
